question: Where did the money in the account come from?
why_it_decides: The origin decides which lawful route exists and whether Chinese tax on the income behind it is still owed. It is the single question the brief does not answer.
how_to_get_it: Bank statements plus the documents behind every large deposit: employment contract and payslips, business accounts and board resolution, the registered property-sale contract, the inheritance notarisation. The bank will ask for the same set.
unlocks: Documented income → L01; home sale → L04; inheritance → L05; pre-emigration property → L06; gift or undocumented → no verified route (U07)

question: Has Chinese individual income tax been paid on it — do you hold a tax payment certificate?
why_it_decides: Chinese tax attaches to the income when it is earned, not to the conversion. If it was never withheld it is owed whether or not the money moves, and the bank needs tax evidence before it will sell the foreign currency.
status: Open — no receipt or amount produced
how_to_get_it: Pull your own record from the personal tax portal or ask the tax service hall (办税服务厅) for a 完税证明 / 纳税记录 for the relevant years. The certificate is a required document on several routes.
unlocks: If paid → the remaining cost is the bank's 0.2%–0.5%; if not → 3%–45% on wages, or 20% flat on dividends, rent and property gains

question: Is the balance RMB, or is some of it already U.S. dollars in a foreign-currency account?
why_it_decides: Foreign currency already in a Chinese foreign-currency account can be wired out on your passport alone. RMB has to be bought with documents first. At $10,000 the two routes differ by a factor of about 1.6; at $400,000 by about 15.
how_to_get_it: Ask the bank for an account statement that shows the currency of each sub-account and the balance in each.
unlocks: Foreign currency → L03 (wire only); RMB → L01 (convert and wire)

question: Do you hold a PRC Foreign Permanent Resident ID card?
why_it_decides: Only holders of that card get the USD 50,000-a-year convenience amount. A U.S. passport alone does not carry it, which is why the usual “USD 50,000 a year” advice does not apply to you.
how_to_get_it: A U.S. citizen without the card: this route is closed. With the card, the annual amount applies on the card alone.
unlocks: No → L07 unavailable; use the documents route (L01) or a property/inheritance route

question: Are you a Chinese tax resident (domicile, or 183 days in the year)?
why_it_decides: It decides whether the U.S.–China treaty applies to you and how China taxes the income. The treaty caps Chinese dividend tax at 10%, but only for a U.S. resident who is not also a Chinese resident under the tie-breaker.
status: Open — depends on domicile and days
how_to_get_it: Count the days in China in the tax year and establish whether you have a domicile (住所) there. If both states claim residence, treaty Article 4(2) leaves it to the competent authorities.
unlocks: Treaty relief available → dividend tax at 10% instead of 20%

question: Did you bring foreign currency into China and convert it to RMB within the last 24 months — and do you still have the exchange slips?
why_it_decides: Unused RMB can be changed back with the passport and the original exchange slip, but the slip is valid for 24 months from the exchange date.
how_to_get_it: Find the 结汇/兑换水单 from the bank. Without the slip the 24-month route is gone; same-day amounts up to USD 500 need only the passport.
unlocks: L02 change-back route, with no source-of-funds file

question: Did you emigrate from China and cancel your Chinese hukou, with the assets held before you left?
why_it_decides: Emigrant property transfer is the route for pre-emigration assets. It needs SAFE approval at the former hukou location, the hukou-cancellation certificate and the tax certificate, and the approval is issued for that one transaction only.
how_to_get_it: Former hukou police station for the 户籍注销证明; the SAFE provincial branch for the application (20 working days, no fee). The approval document 核准件 is valid 当次 — this transaction only.

question: Is the money inside a company you own, rather than in your personal account?
why_it_decides: Company profit has to be paid out as a dividend before it can be remitted. Dividend tax is a flat 20% under domestic law, capped at 10% by treaty if relief is claimed properly.
how_to_get_it: Company documents: articles, the board or shareholder resolution declaring the dividend, the accounts, and the tax filing. Treaty relief needs the information report form plus a U.S. residency certificate.
unlocks: L09 dividend route, and the 10% treaty cap on Chinese tax

question: Did the total of your foreign financial accounts exceed USD 10,000 at any time in the calendar year?
why_it_decides: A U.S. person must file an FBAR for that year. It carries no tax, but the civil ceiling is USD 16,536 for a non-willful miss and, for a willful miss, the greater of USD 165,353 or 50% of the account balance.
how_to_get_it: Add up the maximum value of every foreign account (including this Chinese account) at any point in the year. If the total ever went above USD 10,000, file FinCEN Form 114.

question: Do your specified foreign financial assets cross the Form 8938 threshold?
why_it_decides: Form 8938 is a separate obligation filed with the return. For an unmarried individual living in the U.S. the threshold is more than USD 50,000 on the last day of the year or more than USD 75,000 at any time; living abroad it is USD 200,000 / USD 300,000.
how_to_get_it: Take the year-end and peak values from statements. Form 8938 does not replace the FBAR, and the FBAR does not replace it.

question: When did you acquire the RMB, and at what rate?
why_it_decides: Selling RMB for dollars is a disposition of foreign currency. The gain is ordinary income measured from your acquisition cost; at the 2024 IRS average rate the gain on $400,000 is about $27,700 at today's board.
how_to_get_it: Find the dates and amounts of each acquisition (salary credits, conversions, transfers in) and the rate on each date. The IRS accepts any consistently used posted rate.
unlocks: Section 988 currency gain, or the USD 200 personal-transaction exception if it applies (U05)

question: Will any part of the money cross a border as cash?
why_it_decides: Cash has its own limits and its own forms. China: USD 5,000 or less passes, USD 5,000–10,000 needs a bank carrying permit, above USD 10,000 in principle needs a SAFE permit. U.S.: more than USD 10,000 must be reported on FinCEN Form 105 or it can be seized.
how_to_get_it: Do not carry it. If you must, obtain the permits first and declare on arrival.
unlocks: Cash route limits and FinCEN Form 105
